name: Clean Guitar Shimmer
description: The second button a little slower and deeper, a touch less wet: a clean electric guitar's arpeggios spread across the speakers and shimmer, as the chorus pedals of the same years did.

name: Fast Vibrato
description: Both buttons together: a quick, shallow wobble in both lines at once, more vibrato than chorus, and with the mix at the wet end a pitch vibrato on its own. For organ-like and electric-piano patches.

name: Hissy Original
description: The first button with the lines' own hiss, as an unrestored unit has it, and a little more drive into them for their second harmonic: the old chorus with its faults.

name: Narrow Bass Chorus
description: The slow sweep with the width at a third and less wet: movement on a synth bass that stays in the middle of the mix, so the low end does not go wide.

name: Seasick
description: The slow sweep at twice its depth and a little slower, all wet: the pitch bends up and down in opposite directions on the two sides, a detuned, tape-like wobble.

name: Strings II
description: The second button: the faster sweep, which thickens a string patch or a brass stab into an ensemble without sounding seasick.

name: Subtle Widening
description: The slow sweep at half its depth and a quarter of the mix: a mono source is given width and a little air without being heard as chorus. For a vocal double, a mono synth, or a bus.

name: Synth Pad I
description: The first button as the unit has it: the slow sweep, half dry and half wet, the two lines moving against each other. The wide, gently moving pad of the early 1980s polysynths, on a sawtooth or a square.
